papers.title: Mechanical Properties and In Situ Deformation Imaging of Microlattices Manufactured by Laser Based Powder Bed Fusion.
papers.abstract: This paper reports on the production and mechanical properties of Ti6Al4V microlattice structures with strut thickness nearing the single-track width of the laser-based powder bed fusion (LPBF) system used. Besides providing new information on the mechanical properties and manufacturability of such thin-strut lattices, this paper also reports on the in situ deformation imaging of microlattice structures with six unit cells in every direction. LPBF lattices are of interest for medical implants due to the possibility of creating structures with an elastic modulus close to that of the bones and small pore sizes that allow effective osseointegration. In this work, four different cubes were produced using laser powder bed fusion and subsequently analyzed using microCT, compression testing, and one selected lattice was subjected to in situ microCT imaging during compression. The in situ imaging was performed at four steps during yielding. The results indicate that mechanical performance (elastic modulus and strength) correlate well with actual density and that this performance is remarkably good despite the high roughness and irregularity of the struts at this scale. In situ yielding is visually illustrated.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接涉及LPBF制造的Ti6Al4V点阵结构的力学性能，与用户研究的医用植入物刚度匹配和力学测试高度相关。
llm.why_not_core: Does not cover fatigue testing, detailed surface roughness quantification, or direct osseointegration experiments.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究薄杆Ti6Al4V点阵结构的力学性能及变形行为，以用于医用植入物。
summary_zh.method: 通过LPBF制造四种点阵，结合microCT、压缩测试和原位成像分析。
summary_zh.result: 力学性能与密度高度相关，尽管杆件粗糙，性能仍良好。
summary_zh.validation: 压缩力学测试和原位显微CT成像验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the mechanical properties and deformation of thin-strut Ti6Al4V microlattices for potential biomedical implant applications.
summary_en.method: Four lattices were fabricated by LPBF and characterized via microCT, compression testing, and in situ microCT imaging during yielding.
summary_en.result: Mechanical performance correlates well with actual density; despite high strut roughness, properties are good.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing and in situ microCT imaging during compression.
